solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Run into spring haze in game

parts.note: to spring is to leap

indicators.note: into says the run's letter goes inside the word for haze

parts.note: a haze is a fog
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A runner charges into a springtime mist during some game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' signals that the run abbreviation goes inside the haze word; 'spring' is the leap, not the season.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's game in which players vault over each other's bent backs.

clue.text: Dear rival affected performer

parts.note: luv is a colloquial spelling of love, a British term of endearment
to vie is to compete as a rival

explanation.surface: A darling rival turns out to be a show-off actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dear' is the British endearment 'luv'.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a gushing, theatrical actor, mocking their affectation.

clue.text: Strongman to be seen on time, or after long wait?

parts.note: Atlas was the titan who held up the heavens, a byword for strength

explanation.surface: A strongman turns up on time, or late after a long wait.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so ATLAS sits over T.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom said in relief when something finally happens after a delay.

clue.text: Criminal strike in sport

definitions.meaning: a criminal who handles and sells stolen goods
to strike with a foil or sword in the sport of swordplay

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer lashes out during a game.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a receiver of stolen goods; the verb means to fight with swords.

clue.text: Deluded character nearly put in dictionary left out

indicators.note: put in means the trimmed name goes inside the dictionary letters

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

indicators.note: nearly means the name loses its last letter

parts.note: Walter Mitty is the daydreaming fantasist of a James Thurber story

explanation.surface: A fantasist almost got into the dictionary but was excluded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' drops the last letter of the fantasist's surname; 'put in' places what is left inside the dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: excluded or not included.

clue.text: Sing in Western ball forgoing money

indicators.note: forgoing means doing without, so the money letter is dropped from the ball word

parts.note: a marble is a small glass ball
M is short for money, as in £5m

explanation.surface: Someone sings at a cowboy-themed dance that is free to attend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgoing' drops the money abbreviation; 'ball' is a glass toy, not a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: To warble is to sing with trills, as a songbird does.

clue.text: Charge by convention for instrument

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two parts sit side by side

parts.note: an accord is an agreement or convention
an ion is a particle with an electric charge

explanation.surface: A fee set by custom for a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' suggests a fee but stands for a charged particle.
explanation.definitionFit: A bellows-driven musical instrument with keys or buttons.

clue.text: Very prosperous with first of lots invested?

indicators.note: invested means placed inside, so the letter goes into the prosperous word

parts.note: booming means thriving, prosperous

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of lots

explanation.surface: Someone did very well after putting the first of many sums into stocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested' puts L inside BOOMING. 'Very prosperous' looks like one phrase but splits after 'Very'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild British intensifier, as in 'it's flipping cold', meaning extremely.

clue.text: Car teen trashed round street's end in dramatic interlude

indicators.note: round means the jumbled letters surround the next piece
trashed means wrecked, so these letters are rearranged
end, after street's, picks out the final letter of that word

explanation.surface: A teenager wrecks a car on a street corner in a theatrical scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trashed' rearranges CAR TEEN, and 'round' puts it around T.
explanation.definitionFit: An interval between acts of a play, or music played during it.

clue.text: Venial act almost disrupted foreign city

indicators.note: disrupted means the letters are thrown into a new order
almost means the word act loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A minor sin, nearly committed, upset things in a city abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts ACT to AC; 'disrupted' rearranges VENIAL plus AC.
explanation.definitionFit: Valencia is a large port city on the east coast of Spain.

clue.text: Embody in practise a cold solicitor

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a tout is someone who solicits custom or sells tickets

explanation.surface: A chilly lawyer puts something into practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' looks like a lawyer, but here it is one who solicits business: a tout.
explanation.definitionFit: To act something out is to perform or enact it, giving it physical form.

clue.text: Feature of plates near chocolate boxes

indicators.note: boxes means the words contain the answer within them

explanation.surface: Something on dishes placed close to some chocolates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plates' is rhyming slang: plates of meat means feet.
explanation.definitionFit: The curved underside of the foot, a feature of the feet.

clue.text: Arresting sort enthusiastic about special muscle? Right

indicators.note: about means the enthusiastic word goes round the next pieces

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it
a pec is a chest muscle, short for pectoral

explanation.surface: A striking person keen on a particular muscle, in a fitness-mad scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the keen word round special plus muscle; 'Arresting' means making arrests, not striking.
explanation.definitionFit: A police officer whose job includes arresting people.

clue.text: English city first to last taken with a dance

indicators.note: first to last means the opening letter is moved to the end of the city name

parts.note: Brum is the informal name for Birmingham, a large city in the English Midlands

explanation.surface: An English city is the first to adopt a dance craze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to last' moves the B of BRUM to the end, giving RUMB, then A is added.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a ballroom dance of Cuban origin.

clue.text: NI party's put back source of chips

indicators.note: put back means the letters are written in reverse order

parts.note: the DUP, the Democratic Unionist Party, is a Northern Ireland party; with 's it gives DUPS

explanation.surface: A Northern Irish political party has its plans delayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' reverses DUPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Chips are cut from potatoes, and this is a slang word for a potato.

clue.text: Supreme ride for a tough soldier?

indicators.note: for a means the ride belongs to the soldier, so the soldier comes first

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a tough airborne soldier
a mount is a horse to ride

explanation.surface: The ultimate horse for a hardened soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: The ride is a mount belonging to a para, so PARA comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: highest in rank or importance.

clue.text: Musical figure suffers setback in shock coverage

parts.note: Hair is the famous 1960s rock musical

indicators.note: suffers setback means the number is turned backwards

parts.note: ten is a figure, a number

explanation.surface: A star of a stage show suffers a reversal, which comes as a shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffers setback' turns the number round. 'shock' is a thick mass of hair, not a surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: This mesh covers and holds in place a shock, that is a thick mass, of hair.

clue.text: Senior side adopting one of four in team

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the senior and side letters wrap the quadruplet

parts.note: a quad is one of quadruplets, four born together
on is the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: An older team takes on one of a set of quadruplets as a player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopting' puts the quadruplet inside the senior abbreviation; 'side' is the cricket on side.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of aircraft or soldiers working together as a group.

clue.text: Trumpeter getting point with seconds to go in competition

parts.note: Miles Davis was a famous jazz trumpeter

indicators.note: to go means the seconds letter is removed

parts.note: a cusp is a point

explanation.surface: A trumpeter makes a point with seconds left in a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go' takes S out of CUSP, leaving CUP.
explanation.definitionFit: An international team tennis tournament for men's national sides.

clue.text: What's hunted endlessly by the Spanish in dispute

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: quarry is the prey being hunted
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Spanish hunters argue endlessly over their prey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the final letter of the prey word before the Spanish article.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an argument or row between people.

clue.text: Flier's prank

definitions.meaning: a flier is a bird, here a skylark; the 's stands for is, linking the two
a jape or bit of fun

explanation.surface: A pilot's practical joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a songbird that flies high and a jape or frolic.

clue.text: Some row in English port, maybe

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out in an English harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like a harbour but is the fortified drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Port is a fortified drink from Portugal, so it is one example of the category.

clue.text: Fancy appearing with a feeble expression!

parts.note: a whim is a fancy, a passing desire
per means a, as in so much per head

explanation.surface: Someone's notion turns out to be a weak cry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' looks like a mere article but stands for PER, as in prices 'a head'.
explanation.definitionFit: A weak, low cry: a feeble vocal sound.

clue.text: Expert exploring drives left Spain for brutal place

parts.note: Carl Jung was a psychologist who studied human drives
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A driving expert leaves Spain for a savage spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drives' looks like motoring but means psychological urges.
explanation.definitionFit: A place of ruthless struggle, as in the idiom about it being wild out there.

clue.text: Curtail principal longing to be elevated poet

indicators.note: curtail means cut off the tail, the last letter

parts.note: a head is the principal of a school

indicators.note: to be elevated means raised, so in this down clue the word reads upwards

parts.note: a yen is a longing

explanation.surface: A school head's ambition to be promoted is cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curtail' cuts HEAD to HEA; 'to be elevated' reverses YEN to NEY, upwards in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Seamus, the Nobel-winning Irish poet, is an example.

clue.text: American to dismiss British dependency? It goes without saying

parts.note: ax is the American spelling of axe, to sack someone
IOM is the Isle of Man, a Crown dependency in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: An American cutting loose a British territory: obviously true, no need to say it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is not part of the UK but a self-governing Crown dependency.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-evident truth that needs no proof or argument.

clue.text: Period overseeing fruit mentioned in outdoor assessment?

indicators.note: mentioned means the words are spoken, so their sound counts

parts.note: a reign is a period of rule, and it sits before gage, a greengage plum

explanation.surface: A season's oversight of the fruit crop is talked about in an open-air evaluation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overseeing' simply places REIGN before GAGE, a greengage plum.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument that measures rainfall outdoors, so it assesses the weather.

clue.text: Eat on move in Essex town, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: Grays is a town in Essex, a county east of London

explanation.surface: Snacking while walking around an Essex town.
explanation.definitionFit: To graze is to eat small amounts while moving about, as cattle do.

clue.text: Make good writer in rugby programmes initially

indicators.note: in places the writer inside the rugby letters

parts.note: RU is short for rugby union
Umberto Eco was an Italian novelist

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of programmes

explanation.surface: A writer's work in rugby programmes makes up for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' splits the rugby union letters around the novelist Umberto's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to recover losses, compensating for what was lost.

clue.text: Drops much unpleasant material, graffiti artist's recourse?

parts.note: a spray is a mass of small drops

indicators.note: much means most but not all of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: gunk is sticky, nasty stuff

explanation.surface: Lots of drips and nasty mess: what a graffiti tagger resorts to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'much' trims GUNK to GUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A paint-spraying tool, which a graffiti artist might use on walls.

clue.text: It's in short close to enthralling cat?

definitions.text: It's in short close to enthralling cat?

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the trimmed word goes round the cat
short means the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: close to means near
a cat is a household pet

explanation.surface: A riddle: the thing that captivates a cat when it is close by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims the word for close to; 'enthralling' holds the cat inside it. The whole clue also defines a plant that enthrals a nearby cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The botanical genus of catmint, a plant whose scent fascinates cats.

clue.text: Novelist before turn of year leaves, say

parts.note: Graham Greene was an English novelist

indicators.note: turn of means the year abbreviation is turned round

explanation.surface: A writer departs before the year is out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn of' reverses the year abbreviation. 'leaves' looks like a verb but is foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaves are an example of green foliage and plant growth.
